passages: This little dog is running in a wheel on the kitchen wall. And every step he takes is cooking tonight's dinner!
In old British kitchens, meat roasted on a long iron spit in front of the fire, and somebody had to turn it for hours. So they used a dog.
You see, it's like a hamster wheel hooked to a bike chain. The dog walks, the wheel turns, and a chain carries that motion down to a pulley on the spit, so the roast spins evenly.
There was even a special breed for the job, short legs and a long body, called the turnspit dog. Kitchens often kept two, so they could take turns.
Then cheap clockwork roasting jacks came along, and by around 1900 the breed had disappeared. Only one is known to survive, a stuffed turnspit named Whiskey, in a museum in Wales.
